سَمَامَةٌ : see سَمَامٌ, in three places: ＝
-A2- and see سُمْسُمٌ. ＝
-A3- Also A certain feather, (دَائِرَة, M, K, TA,) which is approved (K, TA) by the Arabs, (TA,) in the neck of the horse, (K,) in the middle of the neck of the horse, (M,) or in the side of his neck. (TA.) ＝
-A4- And The شَخْص [or corporeal form or figure, or person,] (M, K,) of a man: (K:) or, as some say, (M, but accord. to the K “ and ”) the aspect; (M, K;) as in the saying, هُوَ بَهِىُّ السَّمَامَةِ [He is beautiful, or pleasing, in aspect]. (TA.) ―
-b2- And A portion standing up of ruined dwellings. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
